# Atmos Gallery

> A free desktop web tool that reads a colour palette from an image: the mood its light and
> atmosphere carry, not only its dominant colours. Made by KauStudio. Extraction runs in the
> browser: the full-size image is never uploaded, and palettes are stored on the visitor's own
> machine.

This file exists because the site is client-rendered. Agents that do not execute JavaScript receive
an empty body from the homepage, so the description of the tool lives here in full rather than being
something only a browser can discover.

## What it does

- Extracts a colour palette from an image by clustering its pixels in OKLab, on the visitor's own
  machine. The image is read into a canvas and discarded, and the full-size image never leaves the
  machine — see the one stated exception below.
- Names and describes the palette's mood from a fixed descriptive vocabulary (see the taxonomy in
  the repository), across six dimensions: temperature, lightness, chroma, contrast, hue spread and
  dominance.
- Checks WCAG contrast across the palette, pairwise, for AA and AAA at normal and large sizes.
- Builds OKLCH colour harmonies, gamut-mapped back into sRGB.
- Exports a palette as a Tailwind theme block, W3C design tokens, Figma variables, CSS custom
  properties, or a binary `.ase` swatch file.
- Keeps a library in the browser's own storage, with Back up and Restore writing and reading a
  portable JSON file for moving it between machines.

## Facts worth stating plainly

- **Free.** No account, no payment, no trial.
- **Desktop.** A narrow viewport shows a read-only view of a shared palette rather than the tool.
- **The image stays local.** Palette extraction runs on the visitor's machine and the full-size image
  is never uploaded. One exception, stated because it is the only one: naming and describing a
  palette sends a ~320 px thumbnail and the hex values to Anthropic's API, and falls back to a local
  reading if that is unavailable. Shared links carry the palette in the URL fragment, which browsers
  never transmit to a server.
- **No cookies.** The site sets none. Measurement is Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights, both
  cookieless and aggregated.
- **Colour readings are interpretations, not measurements**, and are not colour-managed. They should
  not be relied on for print production, brand matching or any colour-critical work.

## Pages

- [Atmos Gallery](https://atmos.gallery/): the tool itself.
- [About](https://atmos.gallery/about): the long-form argument — why an image's atmosphere is read
  rather than its most common pixels, how OKLCH and WCAG contrast are used, and how a sampled
  palette is turned into a working colour system with semantic roles. Prerendered in full, so it is
  readable without executing JavaScript.
- [Privacy](https://atmos.gallery/privacy): what is collected, the legal basis, processors and
  transfers, retention, and your rights.
- [Terms](https://atmos.gallery/terms): what the tool does, what stays yours, and what it does
  not promise.
